symptom: FreeBSD (or other guest) disables Large Receive Offload (LRO), but Firecracker keeps sending 1536+ byte segments anyway. Guest virtio-net device hangs.

diagnostic_steps.action: Confirm LRO is being NACKed by the guest driver
diagnostic_steps.expected: off [fixed] when guest doesn't support LRO

diagnostic_steps.action: Capture frame sizes Firecracker is sending
diagnostic_steps.expected: Frames >1500 bytes (LRO-aggregated) when guest expects MTU-sized only

fix_steps.action: Track upstream issue #3905; upgrade to a Firecracker version with the LRO-respect fix
fix_steps.command: Monitor github.com/firecracker-microvm/firecracker/issues/3905; update binary when fixed

fix_steps.action: Workaround: switch guest OS to Linux which advertises LRO support
fix_steps.command: Replace FreeBSD guest image with Linux

symptom: Firecracker fails to attach a TAP device with EPERM. Running uid lacks CAP_NET_ADMIN.

diagnostic_steps.expected: CAP_NET_ADMIN should be present (or TAP must be pre-created by privileged user)

diagnostic_steps.action: Verify TAP exists and is accessible
diagnostic_steps.expected: TAP exists; /dev/net/tun rw for uid

fix_steps.action: Pre-create TAP under privileged user; Firecracker only opens, doesn't create
fix_steps.command: sudo ip tuntap add <tap> mode tap user <fc-uid>; sudo ip link set <tap> up

fix_steps.action: Or grant CAP_NET_ADMIN to the binary (less secure)
fix_steps.command: sudo setcap cap_net_admin+ep /usr/bin/firecracker

symptom: Guest can't reach the internet through the host. Packets from the TAP never make it to the egress interface. Host has IPv4 forwarding disabled.

diagnostic_steps.expected: Should be 1; if 0 → root cause

diagnostic_steps.action: Trace whether packets reach the TAP
diagnostic_steps.expected: Outbound packets visible from guest

fix_steps.action: Enable IPv4 forwarding (runtime + persistent)
fix_steps.command: echo 1 | sudo tee /proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_forward; echo 'net.ipv4.ip_forward=1' | sudo tee -a /etc/sysctl.conf

symptom: Guest packets reach the host's egress interface but have non-routable source IPs. NAT masquerade rule isn't installed.

diagnostic_steps.command: sudo nft list ruleset; OR sudo iptables-nft -t nat -S POSTROUTING
diagnostic_steps.expected: MASQUERADE rule for guest IP/subnet → egress iface
Without MASQUERADE: packets visible with raw guest IP (172.16.x.x — non-routable)

fix_steps.action: Install MASQUERADE rule
fix_steps.command: sudo nft add table firecracker; sudo nft 'add chain firecracker postrouting { type nat hook postrouting priority srcnat; policy accept; }'; sudo nft add rule firecracker postrouting ip saddr <guest-ip> oifname <egress> counter masquerade; sudo nft add rule firecracker filter iifname <tap> oifname <egress> accept

symptom: Guest gets connection-refused or no-route when trying to fetch from MMDS at 169.254.169.254 (or configured IP). Guest hasn't added a route for the MMDS IP.

diagnostic_steps.expected: Should resolve to a network interface
network_interfaces[] non-empty

fix_steps.action: Add route in guest
fix_steps.command: guest$ ip route add <mmds-ip> dev <iface>

fix_steps.action: Make persistent via init script
fix_steps.command: Add the route command to /etc/network/if-up.d or systemd-networkd config

symptom: Untrusted guest workload (e.g., AI agent fetching arbitrary URLs) reads sensitive metadata from MMDS via SSRF. MMDS V1 has no token requirement.

diagnostic_steps.expected: If 'V1' (or absent → defaults to V1) → vulnerability confirmed

diagnostic_steps.action: Check Firecracker metrics for evidence of token abuse
diagnostic_steps.command: Inspect mmds.rx_no_token + mmds.rx_invalid_token counters in metrics output
diagnostic_steps.expected: Non-zero → workloads accessing without tokens

fix_steps.action: Migrate MMDS to V2 (session-token-required)
fix_steps.command: PUT /mmds/config {network_interfaces: [...], version: 'V2', ipv4_address: '169.254.169.254'}
fix_steps.validation: MMDS rejects unauthenticated GETs; rx_no_token metric stops growing for new workloads

fix_steps.action: Audit guest workloads to use the V2 PUT-token-then-GET pattern
fix_steps.command: Update guest tooling to issue PUT /latest/api/token first
fix_steps.validation: Guest reads succeed via tokenized path

symptom: After snapshot restore, MMDS GETs return empty/old data. The MMDS data store is intentionally not persisted across snapshots.

diagnostic_steps.action: Confirm MMDS configuration survived (only data is dropped)
diagnostic_steps.expected: version, network_interfaces, ipv4_address all preserved; data store empty

fix_steps.action: Orchestrator must reseed MMDS after every restore
fix_steps.command: PUT /mmds <fresh-payload> right after PUT /snapshot/load

symptom: VirtIO/net throughput per microVM caps at ~10-15 Gbps despite faster host NIC. TAP backend is single-queue; no IFF_MULTI_QUEUE.

diagnostic_steps.expected: Combined: 1 (single-queue)
Plateau around single-queue limit

fix_steps.action: Scale by adding more microVMs (each with its own TAP)
fix_steps.command: Run N microVMs, distribute load across them

fix_steps.action: Tune host TAP txqueuelen for burst absorption
fix_steps.command: ip link set <tap> txqueuelen 10000

symptom: Network requests larger than the rate-limiter bucket size are silently never permitted — bucket can't accumulate enough tokens for one request.

diagnostic_steps.expected: size should be ≥ max single request size (typically MTU * burst factor)

fix_steps.action: Increase rate limiter bucket size to exceed any single legitimate request
fix_steps.command: PATCH /network-interfaces/<id> {tx_rate_limiter: {bandwidth: {size: <larger>, refill_time: <ms>}}}

symptom: Host initiates vsock CONNECT immediately after InstanceStart but Firecracker closes the host-side socket before the guest agent finishes booting and starts listening.

diagnostic_steps.action: Trace timing — when did guest agent listen vs when did host CONNECT
diagnostic_steps.command: Add timestamp logging on both sides; correlate with FC log
diagnostic_steps.expected: Host CONNECT precedes guest listen by N ms

fix_steps.action: Host should wait for a guest-readiness signal before CONNECT
fix_steps.command: Have guest write a sentinel file or send a vsock packet from a known-listening port; host polls before CONNECT

fix_steps.action: Or implement retry-with-backoff on the host CONNECT side
fix_steps.command: Wrap CONNECT in a 100ms-interval retry loop with max 30s timeout

symptom: Active vsock connection terminates mid-flight with a stream read error — Firecracker fails to read from the backing AF_UNIX stream, possibly because the host peer closed it abruptly.

diagnostic_steps.action: Check FC log for backing-stream errors
diagnostic_steps.expected: Error message identifying the failing channel

diagnostic_steps.action: Inspect host peer process state at the time
diagnostic_steps.expected: Peer may have died

fix_steps.action: Make host peers fault-tolerant — close UDS gracefully on shutdown
fix_steps.command: Wrap UDS use in try/finally; explicit close()
fix_steps.validation: Connections close cleanly on peer exit

fix_steps.action: Implement guest-side reconnect logic
fix_steps.command: Guest agent retries vsock connect on EPIPE / ECONNRESET

symptom: Two restored clones of the same snapshot collide on the same vsock UDS path. Second restore fails (or worse: succeeds and steps on the first clone's UDS).

diagnostic_steps.action: Inspect both clones' configured UDS paths
diagnostic_steps.expected: Same uds_path → collision

fix_steps.action: Use vsock_override on snapshot/load to give each clone a unique UDS path
fix_steps.command: PUT /snapshot/load {..., vsock_override: {uds_path: '/clones/v.sock.<id>'}}
fix_steps.validation: Each clone has its own UDS

fix_steps.action: Use jailer per clone — each gets its own chroot, paths are naturally isolated
fix_steps.command: Wrap each FC in jailer with unique --id (which becomes the chroot leaf)

symptom: Guest doesn't see /dev/vsock. PUT /vsock attached the device on Firecracker side but guest kernel lacks CONFIG_VIRTIO_VSOCKETS.

diagnostic_steps.expected: =y or =m
Char device should exist

fix_steps.action: Rebuild guest kernel with CONFIG_VIRTIO_VSOCKETS=y
fix_steps.command: Edit .config; make olddefconfig; make -j

symptom: PUT /vsock fails with ENOENT or ENODEV. Host kernel lacks CONFIG_VHOST_VSOCK module — even though Firecracker bypasses vhost code, the module needs to be loaded.

diagnostic_steps.expected: vhost_vsock available

fix_steps.action: Load the module
fix_steps.command: sudo modprobe vhost_vsock; echo 'vhost_vsock' | sudo tee /etc/modules-load.d/vhost-vsock.conf

symptom: Guest tries to vsock-connect to host CID=2 port N but receives VIRTIO_VSOCK_OP_RST. No process is listening on the host UDS at <uds_path>_<N>.

diagnostic_steps.expected: Listener present (LISTEN state on the UDS)

fix_steps.action: Pre-create the host-side AF_UNIX listener BEFORE guest connects
fix_steps.command: host$ socat - UNIX-LISTEN:<uds_path>_<port>,fork

fix_steps.action: Build a generic per-port spawner on the host (e.g. systemd socket activation on UDS paths)
fix_steps.command: Configure systemd .socket unit for each expected port
